implementation_notes: The Kafka client is the durable store: FutureProducer::send returns a DeliveryFuture that resolves to an OwnedDeliveryResult only when the record was acknowledged (or to a KafkaError when retries were exhausted), so the await point is the send-side acknowledgement and the spool/retry decision belongs in its error arm. enable.idempotence=true (with acks=all) makes retries safe against duplicate writes, and Producer::init_transactions/commit_transaction extend the same guarantee over consume-transform-produce. Idempotence is what replaces the pattern's classic hand-written dedup bookkeeping; a local spool is still needed when the business write and the produce must be atomic.
pitfalls: send() returning Ok only means the record was enqueued; dropping the future or not awaiting it throws the delivery result away.
QueueFull is the one error where the record was definitely not enqueued and a retry is safe - retrying any other error is safe only because idempotence is enabled.

FutureRecord borrows its key and payload: an async task needs the owning variants (FutureRecord::to(&topic).key(&k).payload(&v) with owned buffers moved in), otherwise lifetimes refuse to compile or you clone per retry.
Idempotence is silently dropped by conflicting configuration (acks not all, or an unsupported combination) - rdkafka then behaves like a plain at-most-once producer.

variants.name: lapin publisher confirms over AMQP with durable queues
variants.implementation_notes: With RabbitMQ the store is the broker: declare a durable queue, call Channel::confirm_select, and use the PublisherConfirm future returned by basic_publish - it resolves to Confirmation::Ack only after the broker persisted the message (RabbitMQ confirms a persistent message on a durable queue after writing it to disk). On the consumer side basic_consume yields a Consumer stream whose Delivery values must be acked explicitly, so delivery.ack() after the business commit is the receiver half. Choose it when RabbitMQ is the broker; unlike the Kafka variant there is no broker-side producer idempotence, so deduplication on a message id remains the consumer's responsibility.
pitfalls: The AMQP specification and RabbitMQ discourage sharing a channel across threads - one channel per task, or every publish/confirm future races.
delivery_mode=2 is only persistent on a durable queue; a non-durable queue plus confirms gives a guarantee that ends at the next broker restart.
Dropping the PublisherConfirm future without awaiting it discards the ack (and any error), which is exactly the silent-loss shape the pattern removes.
Auto-recovery replays topology and consumers, not unconfirmed publishes: on reconnect the application decides what to re-publish, and duplicates land on the consumer.
